newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian MP's quiz Di Rupo on new sex child charges.
newsitem.headline: Belgian MP's quiz Di Rupo on new sex child charges.

text.p: Belgian Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo, partially cleared of allegations he had sex with under-age boys, faced questioning by his peers on Tuesday over fresh denunciations.

The Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court and the only one capable of judging a minister, on Monday handed a special parliamentary commission a report on the original allegations against Di Rupo by a sole witness, rejecting them as baseless.

But the Brussels prosecutor who has been compiling the case against the number two figure in Belgium's coalition government has already pulled together another file of allegations, this time anonymous, and spoke on Monday of more to come.

"The second file is very different from the first case. It consists of various items of dubious value," Francophone Socialist member of the commission Serge Moureaux told Reuters just before his party colleague Di Rupo, who denies the charges, appeared to give evidence behind closed doors.
"The second file is even lighter than the first," Flemish Socialist member of the commission Renaat Landuyt told Reuters.

There have been floods of denunciations of all types and against all sorts of people as a tide of hysteria has swamped the country following the discovery in August of an unrelated paedophile ring led by convicted rapist Marc Dutroux.
Last month Marie-France Botte, a prominent child rights campaigner, appealed for calm in the face of what she said were hundreds of letters a day containing all sorts of denunciations.
A police hot line set up in August in the wake of the Dutroux revelations has received thousands of calls -- some of them about Di Rupo.

But just when Di Rupo, a homosexual, might have been able to breathe a little easier following the rejection by the Cour de Cassation of the allegations by the only identified witness, he and Belgian politics received another blow.

Jean-Pierre Grafe, a minister in the francophone community government of the linguistically-divided country who has also been accused of paedophilia, suddenly announced his resignation on the grounds that he could not continue to function in the current over-heated climate. He declared his innocence.

The Cour de Cassation on Tuesday handed a report to the francophone government on the allegations against Grafe, and Belga news agency said chief public prosecutor Eliane Lieckendael had asked for him to be indicted.

Whatever the parliamentary commission decides on Di Rupo -- to reject the allegations, to uphold them and indict him or to ask for more investigations -- must then go to the full parliament to be put to the vote.
The affair has been another nail in the coffin of Belgian public confidence, shaken since the arrest of Dutroux, the subsequent rescue of two young girls and the discovery of the bodies of four more.

In October more than 250,000 people took to the streets of Brussels in support of the victims and their families in a demonstration that crossed the country's language divide and rapidly turned into a show of anger at the system.
